document_title: Driver Check In App — Administrative Module: Driver Check In Set Up Page in HIVE
source_summary: An admin configuration page within The Hive WMS that allows facility administrators to set up and manage the driver check-in process, including toggling check-in steps, configuring temperature and early arrival rules, generating QR codes for mobile access, and customizing confirmation messages — all scoped per organization/facility.

functional_requirements.title: Driver Check In Admin Page Navigation
functional_requirements.description: The Driver Check In Admin page must be accessible from the HIVE Administration menu as a dropdown option labeled 'Driver Check In Set Up'. Selecting it opens a new HIVE tab with page title and tab name 'Driver Check In Admin'.

citation.source_reference: Verify the Driver Check In Admin Page is available in HIVE system under Administration menu: Dropdown option: Driver Check In Set Up...a separate 'Driver Check In Admin' HIVE page is opened in a new HIVE tab. Page title and Tab Name: Driver Check In Admin

functional_requirements.reasoning: Navigation and page structure is a distinct testable capability. Must-Have because it's the entry point for all other features.

functional_requirements.title: Settings List with Toggle Controls
functional_requirements.description: The admin page must display a list of 10 configurable settings, each with: a setting name (label), a toggle control (ON/OFF), an optional input field, and an optional action button. When a toggle is OFF, the setting is disabled both on the admin page and in the Driver Check In mobile app for the selected organization.

citation.source_reference: the Driver Check In Admin Page consists of the list of settings which can be enabled or disabled by toggle...Each Setting in the list includes: Setting name (label), Setting control toggle, Input field near setting name (optional), action button (optional)...When disabled (toggle is in OFF position), the setting is disabled both on Admin page and in Driver Check In Mobile app

functional_requirements.reasoning: Core page structure. Separated from individual settings because the toggle framework is a reusable pattern. Must-Have as it's the foundation for all settings.

functional_requirements.title: Organization Name Setting
functional_requirements.description: Display an Organization Name setting with: toggle always ON and disabled (not editable), a text input field that is disabled and pre-populated with the organization name from the logged-in user's context.

citation.source_reference: Organization Name setting: Toggle is in On position by default, toggle is always disabled. Text input field, disabled. Value is pre-populated based on the User login (organization under user login)

functional_requirements.reasoning: Separate FR because it has unique behavior (always locked, pre-populated from user context). Must-Have as it identifies the facility scope.

functional_requirements.title: QR Code Check In Access Setting with Generate Action
functional_requirements.description: Display a QR Code Check In Access setting with: toggle ON by default (active/editable), and a 'Generate QR Code' action button that is always active regardless of toggle state.

citation.source_reference: QR Code Check In Access setting: Toggle is in ON position by default. Action button 'Generate QR Code': Always active
citation.source_location: Acceptance Criteria — AC#4, QR Code Check In Access

functional_requirements.reasoning: Separated from QR modal (FR-12) because the setting toggle and the generation action are distinct capabilities.

functional_requirements.title: Driver Identity Settings (Name, ID, Phone, Truck)
functional_requirements.description: Display four driver identity settings: Driver Name (toggle ON, always disabled), Driver ID (toggle ON, active/editable), Driver Phone Number (toggle ON, always disabled), Truck Number (toggle ON, always disabled). These control which fields are required during mobile check-in.

citation.source_reference: Driver Name setting: Toggle is in ON position by default, toggle is always disabled. Driver Id setting: Toggle is in ON position by default, toggle is active. Driver Phone Number setting: Toggle is in ON position by default, toggle is always disabled. Truck Number setting: Toggle is in ON position by default, toggle is always disabled

functional_requirements.reasoning: Grouped as one FR because they share the same simple toggle pattern with no input fields. Only Driver ID has an active toggle; the other three are locked ON.

functional_requirements.title: Carrier Approval Step Setting
functional_requirements.description: Display a Carrier Approval Step setting with: toggle ON by default, toggle is active (can be turned OFF to skip carrier approval during mobile check-in).

citation.source_reference: Carrier Approval Step setting: Toggle is in ON position by default, toggle is active
citation.source_location: Acceptance Criteria — AC#4, Carrier Approval Step

functional_requirements.reasoning: Separate FR because it controls a distinct check-in workflow step.

functional_requirements.title: Temperature Acknowledgement Step Setting with Input
functional_requirements.description: Display a Temperature Acknowledgement Step setting with: toggle OFF by default (active). When ON, enable a Temperature Range Requirements input field. Input: alphanumeric, empty by default, required when toggle is ON. Validation on focus out: 'Invalid format' for bad input, 'A value is required' if empty. Auto-save on focus out. Help text displayed below the field.

citation.source_reference: Temperature Acknowledgement Step setting: Toggle is in OFF position by default, toggle is active. Temperature Range Requirements input field: Disabled by default, becomes active if toggle is in ON position. Input format: alphanumeric...Validation error on FE: Invalid format. Validation error on FE if empty: A value is required. Validation is on focus out. The field text edit is saved automatically on focus out
citation.source_location: Acceptance Criteria — AC#4, Temperature Acknowledgement Step

functional_requirements.reasoning: Separate FR because it has complex behavior: conditional input enablement, two validation rules, auto-save, and help text.

functional_requirements.title: Early Check In Step Setting with Hours and Instruction Inputs
functional_requirements.description: Display an Early Check In Step setting with: toggle OFF by default (active). When ON, enable two input fields: (1) Allowed Early Check In Hours — numbers only, required, validation 'Numbers only' and 'A value is required' on focus out. (2) Early Check In Instruction — free text, required, default value provided, validation 'A value is required' on focus out, auto-save on focus out. Help text displayed for both fields.

citation.source_reference: Early Check In Step setting: Toggle is in OFF position by default, toggle is active. Allowed Early Check In Hours input field: numbers only...Early Check In Instruction...Default input value: 'Due to earlier arrival time, you cannot check in via regular process...'
citation.source_location: Acceptance Criteria — AC#4, Early Check In Step

functional_requirements.reasoning: Separate FR because it has the most complex behavior: two conditional inputs with different validation rules, default text with placeholder variable {TRAFFIC_CLERK_PHONE}, and auto-save.

functional_requirements.title: Confirmation Step Setting with Customizable Text
functional_requirements.description: Display a Confirmation Step setting with: toggle ON by default (active). When ON, enable a Successful Check In Confirmation Text input field — free text, required, default value 'Driver Check In is successfully completed! Please wait for the call from Traffic Clerk for Dock assignment and further instructions'. Validation 'A value is required' if empty on focus out. Auto-save on focus out. Help text displayed.

citation.source_reference: Confirmation Step settings: Toggle is in ON position by default, toggle is active. Successful Check In Confirmation Text input field: Enabled by default...Default input value: 'Driver Check In is successfully completed!...'

functional_requirements.reasoning: Separate FR because it has a unique default-ON behavior (input enabled by default, disabled when toggle OFF — inverse of Temperature and Early Check In).

functional_requirements.title: Auto-Save on Focus Out
functional_requirements.description: All text input fields on the admin page must auto-save their values when the user moves focus away from the field (focus out event). No explicit save button is required. Save must persist the value to the backend for the selected organization.

citation.source_reference: The field text edit is saved automatically on focus out (mentioned for Temperature, Early Check In Instruction, and Confirmation Text)

functional_requirements.reasoning: Extracted as cross-cutting FR because auto-save applies to all text inputs. Must-Have because without it, user changes would be lost.

functional_requirements.title: Frontend Validation on Focus Out
functional_requirements.description: All input fields must validate on focus out (not on keystroke). Validation rules: Temperature Range — 'Invalid format' for non-alphanumeric, 'A value is required' if empty when ON. Early Hours — 'Numbers only' for non-numeric, 'A value is required' if empty when ON. Early Instruction — 'A value is required' if empty when ON. Confirmation Text — 'A value is required' if empty when ON. Validation errors displayed inline below the field.

citation.source_reference: Validation error on FE: Invalid format...Validation error on FE if empty: A value is required...Validation is on focus out (repeated across Temperature, Early Check In, Confirmation settings)

functional_requirements.reasoning: Extracted as cross-cutting FR because validation pattern is consistent across all inputs. Separate from auto-save because validation must run before save.

functional_requirements.title: QR Code Generation Modal
functional_requirements.description: When 'Generate QR Code' button is clicked, display a modal popup with: title 'QR Code for {ORG_NAME} Driver Check In Access' (where ORG_NAME is from the Organization setting), a newly generated QR code, and three action buttons: 'Save as PDF' (auto-downloads PDF file), 'Print' (opens system print dialog), 'Close' (dismisses modal without saving/printing).

citation.source_reference: when the button 'Generate QR Code' is clicked, a pop-up is displayed. Title: 'QR Code for {ORG_NAME} Driver Check In Access'...New generated QR code is displayed. Action buttons: Save as PDF, Print, Close

functional_requirements.reasoning: Separate FR because the QR modal is a distinct UI component with its own actions (PDF generation, print dialog, close). Must-Have for mobile app access.

functional_requirements.title: QR Code PDF Download
functional_requirements.description: When 'Save as PDF' button is clicked in the QR modal, automatically generate and download a PDF file containing the QR code to the user's computer.

citation.source_reference: When 'Save as PDF' button is clicked, a file with QR is automatically generated and saved on User's computer in PDF format

functional_requirements.reasoning: Separate from FR-12 because PDF generation is a distinct technical capability (requires PDF library, file download API).

functional_requirements.title: QR Code Print
functional_requirements.description: When 'Print' button is clicked in the QR modal, open the system's print dialog allowing the user to select a printer and print the QR code.

citation.source_reference: When 'Print' button is clicked, an automatic print pop-up window setting is opened

functional_requirements.reasoning: Separate from FR-13 because print uses browser's window.print() API, different from PDF generation.

functional_requirements.title: Settings Persistence per Organization
functional_requirements.description: All setting toggle states and input field values must be persisted per organization. When an admin user logs in and opens the Driver Check In Admin page, the settings must reflect the previously saved configuration for their organization.

citation.source_reference: set up driver check-in process and view settings according to the facility preferences...the check-in will follow business requirements of particular location

functional_requirements.reasoning: Implied but critical — without persistence, settings would reset on page reload. The user story explicitly mentions 'facility preferences' and 'particular location', implying per-org storage.

functional_requirements.title: Toggle State Sync with Mobile App
functional_requirements.description: When a setting toggle is changed to OFF on the admin page, the corresponding step/field must be disabled in the Driver Check In mobile app for that organization. When toggled ON, the step/field must be enabled in the mobile app.

citation.source_reference: When disabled (toggle is in OFF position), the setting is disabled both on Admin page and in Driver Check In Mobile app for selected organization

functional_requirements.reasoning: Critical integration requirement — the admin page controls mobile app behavior. Must-Have because without it, the admin page has no effect.

functional_requirements.title: User Authentication and Session Management
functional_requirements.description: Users must authenticate via email/password or SSO to access the HIVE system. Sessions managed with secure tokens. Admin role required for Driver Check In Admin page access.

citation.source_reference: As an Admin HIVE User — implies authenticated user with Admin role

functional_requirements.reasoning: Greenfield build requires authentication. Source implies authenticated admin users but doesn't specify mechanism.

functional_requirements.title: User Role Management (Admin vs Standard)
functional_requirements.description: Support at least two roles: Admin (can access Driver Check In Admin page and all settings) and Standard User (cannot access admin page). Admin role gates the Administration menu visibility and API access.

citation.source_reference: As an Admin HIVE User — role-based access implied

functional_requirements.reasoning: NFR-04 requires admin-only access. Greenfield needs role management to enforce this.

functional_requirements.title: Organization and Facility Data Model
functional_requirements.description: Maintain an organization/facility data model with: org ID, name, address, and associated users. Each organization has its own set of driver check-in settings. Users are assigned to one or more organizations.

citation.source_reference: Value is pre-populated based on the User login (organization under user login)...disabled both on Admin page and in Driver Check In Mobile app for selected organization

functional_requirements.reasoning: Settings are per-organization. Greenfield needs the org data model to scope settings correctly.

functional_requirements.title: Settings Data Model and Storage
functional_requirements.description: Persist driver check-in settings in a database with: setting_id, organization_id, setting_name, toggle_state (boolean), input_value (text, nullable), updated_at, updated_by. Support all 10 settings per organization.

citation.source_reference: The field text edit is saved automatically on focus out — implies persistent storage

functional_requirements.reasoning: Auto-save and per-org persistence require a data model. Greenfield needs DB schema design.

functional_requirements.title: Settings API — Admin CRUD Endpoints
functional_requirements.description: Provide REST API endpoints for the admin page: GET /api/v1/driver-checkin/settings (read all settings for org), PUT /api/v1/driver-checkin/settings/{setting_id} (update toggle or value). Endpoints require admin authentication.

citation.source_reference: saved automatically on focus out — implies API to persist changes

functional_requirements.reasoning: Frontend auto-save needs backend API. Greenfield needs API design for settings CRUD.

functional_requirements.title: Settings API — Mobile App Read Endpoint
functional_requirements.description: Provide a read-only API endpoint for the mobile app: GET /api/v1/driver-checkin/settings/mobile?org_id={id} returning only enabled settings with their configured values. No admin auth required (mobile app auth).

citation.source_reference: the setting is disabled both on Admin page and in Driver Check In Mobile app for selected organization

functional_requirements.reasoning: Mobile app needs to read settings to know which check-in steps to show. Separate from admin API for security (different auth).

functional_requirements.title: Help Text Display Component
functional_requirements.description: Display contextual help text below configurable settings. Help text is static (defined per setting), shown in a muted style, and linked to the input via aria-describedby for accessibility.

citation.source_reference: Help Text: 'Add the Temperature requirements to display during Check In via mobile app...' (and similar for Early Check In and Confirmation)

functional_requirements.reasoning: Four settings have explicit help text in the source. Greenfield needs a reusable help text component.

functional_requirements.title: Save Confirmation Feedback
functional_requirements.description: After auto-save completes on focus out, display a subtle visual confirmation (e.g., brief checkmark icon or 'Saved' text near the field) that disappears after 2 seconds. On save failure, display an error indicator with retry option.

citation.source_reference: The field text edit is saved automatically on focus out — no explicit feedback specified

functional_requirements.reasoning: Source specifies auto-save but no feedback. Users need confirmation that save succeeded, especially in warehouse environments with unreliable connectivity.

functional_requirements.title: Page Loading State
functional_requirements.description: Display a loading state (skeleton or spinner) while settings are being fetched from the API on page load. Show error state with retry button if the API call fails.

citation.source_reference: Not explicitly stated — implied by page that loads settings from backend

functional_requirements.reasoning: Settings are loaded from API (FR-21). Greenfield needs loading and error states for the initial page load.

functional_requirements.title: QR Code Generation Backend
functional_requirements.description: Backend service to generate a QR code image encoding a URL/deep link for the Driver Check In mobile app, scoped to the organization. QR code must be unique per organization and regenerated on each 'Generate' click.

citation.source_reference: New generated QR code is displayed...QR Code for {ORG_NAME} Driver Check In Access

functional_requirements.reasoning: FR-12 covers the modal UI but the QR image itself needs backend generation. Greenfield needs a QR generation service.

non_functional_requirements.title: Auto-Save Responsiveness
non_functional_requirements.description: Auto-save on focus out must complete within 2 seconds with visual feedback (e.g., subtle save indicator). No blocking UI during save.

citation.source_reference: The field text edit is saved automatically on focus out

non_functional_requirements.reasoning: Source specifies auto-save but no performance target. 2-second target inferred from standard UX expectations for inline save. Must-Have because slow saves would frustrate users.

non_functional_requirements.title: Validation Feedback Timing
non_functional_requirements.description: Validation errors must appear immediately on focus out (within 200ms). Errors must be displayed inline below the field with clear visual indication (red border, error text).

citation.source_reference: Validation is on focus out (repeated for all input fields)

non_functional_requirements.reasoning: Source specifies focus-out validation but no timing. 200ms is standard for perceived-instant feedback.

non_functional_requirements.title: WCAG 2.1 AA Compliance
non_functional_requirements.description: The admin page must meet WCAG 2.1 AA standards: all toggles keyboard-operable, all inputs labeled, validation errors announced by screen readers, modal has focus trap, help text linked via aria-describedby.

citation.source_reference: Not explicitly stated in source

non_functional_requirements.reasoning: Source does not mention accessibility. Flagged as Should-Have based on enterprise standards (EA14 in kb-L1-hive-enterprise-architecture). Gap flagged below.

non_functional_requirements.title: Admin Role Authorization
non_functional_requirements.description: The Driver Check In Admin page must only be accessible to users with Admin role. Non-admin users must not see the menu option or be able to access the page directly.

citation.source_reference: As an Admin HIVE User, I want to be able to set up driver check-in process

non_functional_requirements.reasoning: User story specifies 'Admin HIVE User' — implies role-based access control. Must-Have for security.

constraints.description: Must be implemented within the existing HIVE system as a new page/tab, not a standalone application.

citation.source_reference: set up driver check-in process...directly in HIVE system...a separate 'Driver Check In Admin' HIVE page is opened in a new HIVE tab

constraints.reasoning: The page must integrate into the existing HIVE navigation and tab system, constraining the technology and deployment approach.

constraints.description: Settings must sync with the Driver Check In Mobile app. The admin page controls mobile app behavior per organization.

citation.source_reference: the setting is disabled both on Admin page and in Driver Check In Mobile app for selected organization

constraints.reasoning: Implies an API contract between the admin page and the mobile app. The mobile app must read settings from the same backend.

assumptions.description: The HIVE system already has an Administration menu with dropdown navigation, and the new 'Driver Check In Set Up' option will be added to it.
assumptions.reasoning: Source says 'under Administration menu' but doesn't confirm the menu exists. Greenfield build needs to create or extend this menu.

assumptions.description: The HIVE system supports opening pages in new tabs within the application (not browser tabs).
assumptions.reasoning: Source says 'opened in a new HIVE tab' — this implies an in-app tab system, not browser tabs. Greenfield build needs to implement this tab system.

assumptions.description: The organization name is available from the authenticated user's session/context and does not need to be manually entered.
assumptions.reasoning: Source says 'pre-populated based on the User login (organization under user login)'. Assumes user-org mapping exists in the auth system.

assumptions.description: The QR code, when scanned, opens the Driver Check In mobile app or web page for the specific organization.
assumptions.reasoning: Source describes QR generation but not what the QR code links to. The QR must encode a URL or deep link to the mobile check-in flow for the org.

assumptions.description: The {TRAFFIC_CLERK_PHONE} placeholder in the Early Check In instruction default text will be replaced with an actual phone number from the facility configuration.
assumptions.reasoning: Source uses {TRAFFIC_CLERK_PHONE} as a variable but doesn't specify where this value comes from. Needs a facility phone number field or configuration.

gaps.impact: Cannot ensure the page is usable by users with disabilities or meets compliance standards
gaps.suggested_question: Should the Driver Check In Admin page meet WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards? Are there specific accessibility requirements for HIVE?
gaps.reasoning: Enterprise applications typically require WCAG compliance. Source document makes no mention of accessibility.

gaps.description: No audit logging specified for setting changes
gaps.impact: Cannot track who changed which settings and when — important for compliance and troubleshooting
gaps.suggested_question: Should changes to driver check-in settings be audit-logged (who changed what, when)?
gaps.reasoning: Admin configuration changes in enterprise systems typically require audit trails. Source doesn't mention logging.

gaps.impact: Cannot determine if admins can configure settings for organizations other than their own
gaps.suggested_question: Should admins be able to select and configure different organizations, or only their own? If multi-org, should this be role-based?
gaps.reasoning: Source explicitly marks this as 'TBD with Business: do we want to make an Org field a dropdown and enable editing of different Organizations?'

gaps.impact: Cannot determine if temperature range input needs a unit selector
gaps.suggested_question: Should the Temperature Range Requirements field include a Celsius/Fahrenheit dropdown selector?
gaps.reasoning: Source explicitly marks this as 'TBD with Business: the Celsius and Fahrenheit dropdown option can be added'.

gaps.description: No error handling for backend save failures
gaps.impact: Cannot determine user experience when auto-save fails (network error, server error)
gaps.suggested_question: What should happen if auto-save fails? Show error toast? Retry? Revert the field value?
gaps.reasoning: Source specifies auto-save on focus out but doesn't address failure scenarios. Network issues are common in warehouse environments.

gaps.description: No specification for the QR code content/format
gaps.impact: Cannot implement QR generation without knowing what data to encode
gaps.suggested_question: What URL or data should the QR code encode? A deep link to the mobile app? A web URL? What parameters (org ID, facility ID)?
gaps.reasoning: Source says 'Generate QR Code' but doesn't specify the QR payload. This is critical for the mobile app integration.

gaps.description: No specification for the 'Invalid format' validation rule for Temperature Range
gaps.impact: Cannot implement validation without knowing what constitutes a valid temperature format
gaps.suggested_question: What is a valid temperature range format? Examples: '35-40', '35°F-40°F', '2°C-4°C'? Is it a range (min-max) or a single value?
gaps.reasoning: Source says 'alphanumeric' input with 'Invalid format' validation but doesn't define what a valid format looks like.

gaps.description: No API specification for settings persistence
gaps.impact: Cannot design the backend without knowing the API contract
gaps.suggested_question: What API endpoints should be used? A single PUT /settings endpoint with all values, or individual endpoints per setting? What's the data model?
gaps.reasoning: Greenfield build needs API design. Source only describes the frontend behavior.

gaps.description: Early Check In violation workflow is TBD
gaps.impact: Cannot fully implement the early check-in flow without knowing the violation steps
gaps.suggested_question: What happens after the early check-in instruction is shown to the driver? Can they still check in with a delay? Is there a manual override?
gaps.reasoning: Source explicitly marks this as 'TBD with Business: the text 1 and 2 and violation steps for Early Check In'.

gaps.description: No specification for concurrent editing protection
gaps.impact: If two admins edit settings simultaneously, last-write-wins could cause data loss
gaps.suggested_question: Should the system prevent concurrent editing of the same organization's settings? Optimistic locking? Last-write-wins?
gaps.reasoning: Auto-save on focus out with multiple admins could cause conflicts. Source doesn't address this.
